newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady, sales light-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady, sales light-trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hogs sold at prices steady with Thursday's values in light early trading following the cancellation of Saturday slaughter plans by some meat packing plants, cash livestock dealers said.
The plants cancelled Saturday operations because operating margins turned unprofitable amid higher prices packers were paying for tight hog supplies and lower wholesale pork values, the dealers said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold in the country at $51.50 per cwt and top prices at plants ranged from $52.50 to $53.50. Active corn harvesting restricted runs, sources said.
Illinois hogs sold at $50.50 to $52.00 in the country and $53.00 at plants. Indiana top prices were reported at $50.50 to $51.00 in the country and $51.50 to $52.00 at plants.
Ohio hogs sold at $48.00 to $49.00 in the country and $50.00 to $51.00 at plants, sources there said.

Hog slaughter Friday was estimated from 361,000 to 366,000 head, compared with 362,000 a week ago and 364,000 a year ago. Saturday's slaughter was pegged from 43,000 to 70,000 head, compared with 38,000 a week ago and 188,000 a year ago.
Some cash sources said Saturday's slaughter would be closer to the lower end of the range.
